newsitem.title: USA: US Senator drops objection to Pena at Energy Dept.
newsitem.headline: US Senator drops objection to Pena at Energy Dept.

text.p: A Republican senator Tuesday said he would drop his objection to advancing the nomination of Federico Pena as U.S. energy secretary.

Sen. Rod Grams of Minnesota said he still was concerned by Pena's "continued lack of specific answers" on how to dispose of radioactive waste from nuclear utilities, but Grams said he would no longer object to efforts to hold a full Senate vote to confirm Pena.
Grams said he was lifting his objection because Pena "provided verbal assurances of his commitment that our nuclear waste storage situation is a federal problem, one worthy of a federal solution."

Pena's nomination has been delayed by complaints from several Republican senators that the administration has balked on its responsibility to find a way to store nuclear waste that the federal government takes legal title to next year.
Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski had delayed a committee vote on Pena for several weeks over the issue, but finally held a vote last week in which the panel approved Pena 19-0.

Murkowski, Grams and others are pushing a bill to set up a temporary dump in Nevada for the nuclear waste now stored at more than 70 sites around the country, but the Clinton administration has threatened to veto the bill.
